Learn how to maximize ROI and create successful B2B programmatic advertising campaigns. Get the latest best practices for designing effective campaigns, including targeting methods, budget optimization, and more.

The global programmatic advertising market was valued at [$451.3 billion in 2021](https://www.alliedmarketresearch.com/programmatic-display-advertising-market-A31468) and is expected to increase at a CAGR of 35.8% from 2022 to 2031, reaching $9473.3 billion by 2031.

## Introduction to B2B Programmatic Advertising

B2B Programmatic advertising is an automated approach to buying and selling digital advertising space, allowing for more efficient use of time and resources than traditional methods. B2B programmatic advertising is the same approach, but with a focus on the B2B market. This type of advertising is becoming increasingly popular, as it allows B2B businesses to target their audiences more effectively while providing greater transparency and control over their campaigns.

Additionally, programmatic advertising allows B2B businesses to define their target audience and customize their campaigns to reach them more efficiently. By using [data-driven insights](https://www.s2wmedia.com/data-driven-lead-generation-strategy), B2B programmatic ad networks can help businesses maximize their return on investment in digital advertising.

## What it is, and how it works?

B2B Programmatic advertising is an automated way of buying and selling advertising space in real-time. It eliminates the need for manual processes and instead utilizes automated algorithmic decision-making to purchase digital advertising space across an array of websites. This allows marketers to quickly reach their target audiences while ensuring that the ads are being shown to the right people. With programmatic advertising, marketers can also track the success of their campaigns in real time and make adjustments if needed. By using programmatic advertising, B2B marketers can maximize their exposure and reach their desired audiences more quickly and effectively.

# The Power of Dynamic Ads for Local Advertising

Dynamic Ads have transformed general campaigns into local campaigns that are personalised by outlet, without the need for time-consuming manual work. As a result, Dynamic Ads have proven to be a powerful tool for local advertising. DeepReach decrypts the subject.

[The Power of Dynamic Ads for Local Advertising](https://www.deepreach.com/media/the-power-of-dynamic-ads-for-local-advertising#)

![The Power of Dynamic Ads for Local Advertising](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/62139d0c11fad8c02aaea357/646ce013bce26ed717e28fca_Header%20site%20Dynamic%20Ads.png)

## What is Dynamic Advertising?

Dynamic Advertising, also referred to as Dynamic Creative Optimisation (DCO), is revolutionising the advertising landscape by tailoring messages to specific contexts. By leveraging DCO, marketers can create highly personalised campaigns that resonate with their target audience. This process involves customising advertising content based on various factors, including the user's geographic location, web browsing behaviour, and product availability. As businesses strive to enhance their marketing strategies, the adaptation to the geographical context through DCO is rapidly gaining momentum. It enables advertisers to maximise their reach and engagement by delivering contextually relevant content that captures the attention of potential customers in specific locations.

‍

Ad creatives can differ depending on the location, including elements such as captions, visuals, and prices. It is crucial to adapt the content based on triggers that incorporate changes in messages, images, prices, and other factors determined by the user's location, profile, and other contextual elements.

This technique is gaining popularity as it boosts advertising campaign performance, and it allows the creation of dynamic ads that are tailored to store specific information, stock availability, and product-focused content.

One type of Dynamic Ad is the Dynamic Search Ad, which appears on search engines and is based on website content rather than specific keywords. This ad format saves time as there is no need to map keywords, set up bids, or create ad text for each ad, and it enables marketers to reach audiences beyond the keywords they are already targeting in their campaigns, resulting in additional traffic and increased reach.

Each media platform can have its own unique characteristics, and the integration of advertisements may not necessarily be the same across all platforms. This is what we will explore. Additionally, it is important to pay attention to the dimensions of ad creatives, especially in the case of static advertising on display networks.

‍

The formats used for Dynamic Ads are the same as the standard IAB formats.

The IAB formats refer to advertising banners that can be found on websites, social media platforms, and mobile applications. They can come in various forms such as static images or videos. On the other hand, the interstitial is an advertisement that displays on the entire screen of a device before redirecting the user to the website or application.

‍

### How does Dynamic Advertising work?

It should be noted that there are two things that can be customised from a feed.

*   Texts
*   Images

By leveraging personalisation based on location, product feeds, weather broadcast, stock availability, and population density, businesses can deliver highly tailored experiences to their customers.

The product feed is a structured file containing detailed and specific information about multiple products. The text variable can be a single textual element in a description or on an image that can be integrated into different parts of dynamic or static advertisements.

The product feed is used to manage and synchronise detailed information about multiple products, while the text variable is used to personalise text elements in ads or web pages with specific information, such as a user's name or the current time.

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/62139d0c11fad8c02aaea357/646cbf6751e7b0d2a0b7801b_variable%20text%20dynamic%20ads%20article.png)

‍

‍

The text variable in description can be used on media such as Google, Meta, or Display. It refers to all the elements that can be used in text format (locations, promotions, dates, prices, etc.)

‍

‍

‍

‍

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/62139d0c11fad8c02aaea357/646cbfbcc761445102cdb09c_variable%20product%20feed%20article%20DA.png)

‍

‍

The image is a variable that can also be used across all media. Its creation can be done via HTML5 or with static images using image generation tools. Customisation of the creations can be done directly within the media.

‍

‍

‍

‍

‍

**Good to know**: the retrieved data that enables the customisation of these ads comes from various sources, either from platforms such as DeepReach or from the product feeds of agencies or direct advertisers. We are talking about geographical data, weather data, product feeds, and more.

‍

‍

## Why use Dynamic Ads?

Advertisers can leverage these differences to create more effective and targeted campaigns, modifying creatives based on location and variables to create personalised messages for each user.

Location is one such factor that can influence ad creatives, with variations made to better appeal to the preferences and needs of audiences in specific areas. The variable is another factor, with language and phrasing adjusted to suit the interests and message the advertiser wishes to convey.

‍

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/62139d0c11fad8c02aaea357/646cc0488ac8391a64af6dde_cta%20article%20DA.png)

‍

‍

Furthermore, by utilising feed variables, it is possible to incorporate platform-specific call-to-action buttons, such as "Learn More" or "Shop Now," which significantly enhance user engagement. Additionally, the call to action can be customised to meet specific requirements and objectives locally.

‍

‍

‍

Dynamic Ads offer several benefits, including increased consumer interest, improved brand perception, and greater relevance to user needs. By targeting ads more effectively, they can increase brand revenue and optimise return on advertising spend.

‍

*   depending on store-specific information
*   more focused on product
*   availability of stocks

Dynamic Ads can be used in two ways - remarketing and user acquisition. In remarketing, personalised ads are shown to users who have shown an interest in a particular product or offer. # Programmatic Advertising for Multi-Location Businesses: How to Scale Without Losing Local Impact

![high‑tech, isometric, neon-style image](https://www.postmediasolutions.com/hubfs/Programmatic.png)

In today’s hyper competitive B2C and B2B world, multi-market brands face the combined challenge of maintaining a consistent identity while connecting with diverse local audiences in an authentic way. Programmatic advertising for multi-location businesses is a powerful way to scale campaigns to meet big organizational objectives and specific local goals. 

![high‑tech, isometric, neon-style image](https://www.postmediasolutions.com/hs-fs/hubfs/Programmatic.png?width=1536&name=Programmatic.png "high‑tech, isometric, neon-style image")

  
Research shows that consistent branding can increase revenue by up to [20 per cent.](https://www.marq.com/blog/brand-consistency-competitive-advantage/) But when your brand has multiple locations and touchpoints across those locations, it can be difficult to create compelling messages that are both consistent and customized to meet the needs of your target audience.

That’s where [programmatic advertising](https://www.postmediasolutions.com/en-ca/blog/what-is-programmatic-advertising-and-how-does-it-work) can be a game changer. Programmatic advertising for multi-location businesses shows highly targeted ads to the right audience at the right time at the right touchpoints, supercharging marketing efforts. It offers a powerful way to influence and engage high-intent shoppers, and reinforce and scale online and offline campaigns to meet big organizational objectives and specific local goals.

For brands with multiple locations – both physical and/or digital – programmatic advertising is a critical component of a successful multi-location ad strategy.

[CONNECT WITH A PROGRAMMATIC EXPERT](https://www.postmediasolutions.com/en-ca/contact-us)

## What makes programmatic advertising effective for multi-location brands?

In today’s hyper competitive B2C and B2B world, multi-location brands face the combined challenge of maintaining a consistent identity while connecting with diverse local audiences in an authentic way.

Programmatic advertising is the fully automated, data-driven, real-time buying and selling of digital ad space across multiple websites and networks using artificial intelligence (AI) and real-time bidding.

Programmatic advertising for multi-location businesses combines corporate branding with local tactics – such as precision targeting and geofencing – to deliver highly targeted, personalized, localized ads across numerous channels in real time while maintaining unified brand messaging. It can support multi-market campaigns with live, data-based optimization and dynamic creative optimization.

Importantly, programmatic advertising can do all this while ensuring consistent messaging and audience targeting across platforms.

The result: programmatic advertising for multi-location brands improves efficiency and return on investment (ROI) by targeting high-intent audiences when they are most likely to make a purchase, improving online and in-store engagement and boosting budget efficiency.

## Common challenges in multi-location advertising

How do you make sure your ads work in all your locations when your business operates in multiple markets, each with their own unique identity, competitors and consumer demographics?

The challenge becomes more complex when you factor in the need to identify and align location-specific key performance indicators (KPIs) and data collection methodologies. While it is important to acknowledge that what works in one region might not work in another and allow for differences, without alignment it is difficult to accurately attribute impact to specific campaigns, integrate data and balance overall corporate marketing goals with local needs.

Other common challenges include:

*   Maintaining a consistent brand identity across locations.
*   Managing content across hundreds of screens to avoid duplication, siloed information and outdated material.
*   Proving in-store ROI.
*   Navigating disconnected systems and fragmented processes, which can lead to blind spots and delay ad campaigns.
*   Measuring and optimizing performance.

## How programmatic advertising supports local and national goals

Programmatic advertising for multi-location businesses is the equalizer. By employing a hybrid approach that combines national reach with local precision, programmatic advertising can run simultaneous national campaigns designed to build and reinforce brand visibility, recognition and identity, and local campaigns designed to drive traffic, engagement and conversions in specific locations.

One of the biggest benefits of programmatic advertising for multi-location businesses is the access it provides to centralized reporting, and detailed analytics and metrics – such as impressions, clicks, conversions, foot traffic and revenue attribution – from all locations. This level of transparency and actionable audience and campaign insights allow brands to optimize their creative, budgets and bidding strategies to maximize impact.

## Best practices for programmatic advertising across multiple locations

*   *   Develop detailed profiles of your target audience. Create and deliver personalized ads by integrating the data you’ve collected in your customer relationship management solution across digital interactions and at point of sale, including demographics, interests, shopping behaviour and past purchases. Leverage this information to create and target lookalike audiences, expanding your reach and scaling growth.  
          
        
    *   Establish standardized processes and technology to collect data. Create a framework that ensures all locations collect data uniformly but also have the flexibility to adapt to meet their unique needs. Invest in platforms designed for multi-location businesses. This will ensure information can be integrated seamlessly.  
          
        
    *   Set location-based targeting parameters. Local programmatic advertising uses many location targeting methods, including GPS and IP address targeting, geofencing and beacon technology. To maximize the relevance of your ads, define precise boundaries. Local programmatic platforms also allow brands to include additional targeting criteria, such as demographics and weather conditions.
